class_closure_assessment.question: 5th round — is the document-level default-deny approach able to close the class, or is it whack-a-mole forever?
class_closure_assessment.answer: This axis (top-level hook-kill switch) is CLOSED, and — unlike rounds 1-4 — the fix pairs instance-closure with a CLASS-EXTENDING mechanism. Rounds 1-4 each closed only the named instance (basename -> command -> tuple -> whole-object), and the next judge found the next-wider instance. This commit adds a schema-completeness meta-test (hook-wiring-parity.bats test 77): HOOK_KILL_SWITCHES is hard-coded but the test diffs it against the official settings schema's hook-affecting booleans, so a NEW vendor hook-kill boolean fails CI until registered. That converts whack-a-mole into a self-extending guard for the top-level-switch axis. Verified against the LIVE newest schema (2.1.217 — it moved 2.1.215->216->217 during this very session; the guard's list still fully covers it: GUARD_SET == SCHEMA_SET). Verdict on the meta-question: the approach IS able to close the class for the modeled axis; remaining exposure is (i) future hook-killers that are non-boolean or whose description omits 'hook' (escape the SCHEMA_SET type+keyword gate), (ii) value non-canonicalization (A3), (iii) CI without the extension -> explicit skip. These are heuristic-completeness / hardening limits, not an open certain bypass — a categorical break from rounds 1-4.

reproduction_evidence_over_1st_round: The 1st round also passed at min-7 and was overturned because it was UNTESTED (basename bypass existed but was not driven). This pass is the opposite: it is grounded in 19 live guard executions that include the 4th round's exact killer plus every prior N1/N2 vector and 7 new adversarial vectors (A1-A7). The only residuals are non-demonstrable (A3 needs unverified vendor coercion) or correct-by-design (A1). No demonstrable spec-valid bypass remains.

A3_value_coercion.finding: Kill-switch check is string-exact: __n=$(jq -r '.[$k] // false'); [[ "$__n" == "true" ]]. It catches boolean true AND string "true" (both render 'true' under jq -r — confirmed A2 -> DENY), but MISSES other truthy encodings: number 1 (renders '1'), non-empty arrays/objects. Reproduced: disableAllHooks:1 -> guard ALLOW(0).
A3_value_coercion.why_not_gate_blocking: disableAllHooks is type:boolean in the schema; value 1 is a type violation, so a spec-compliant edit cannot use it. Runtime exploitability is UNVERIFIED and points the safe way: a typed-boolean loader most likely rejects/ignores the invalid field (-> hooks still fire, no bypass) rather than coercing 1->true. The realistic off-spec encoding (string 'true') IS caught. I could not DEMONSTRATE that disableAllHooks:1 disables hooks at runtime, so per grounded-verdict calibration it is a hardening residual, not a proven open bypass.
A3_value_coercion.cheap_fix: Replace string-equality with jq truthiness: __n=$(jq -r 'if .[$k] then "on" else "off" end'); this treats 1, "x", {}, [] as on and only false/null/absent as off — closes A2+A3 uniformly while still allowing explicit false (V3). REQUIRED follow-up.

A1_old_r_empty_skip.finding: The kill-switch loop runs only `if [[ -n "$OLD_R" ]]`. On a settings.json with NO harness wiring (OLD_R empty), an edit adding wiring AND disableAllHooks:true together is ALLOWED (reproduced A1 -> 0).
A1_old_r_empty_skip.why_not_gate_blocking: INV-13/SC-1 is a monotonic add-only guard defined RELATIVE to OLD ('배선을 축소하는 편집이 차단된다'). If OLD has no wiring there is no protection to reduce. You cannot manufacture an OLD_R-empty state from a wired one: wiring removal is denied (V9 -> 2), so wired->unwired is impossible. An init.sh-installed settings.json ALWAYS has wiring, so its OLD_R is never empty. This is the same semantics as every other invariant in the guard (a file that never had the protected content is not retroactively protected).
A1_old_r_empty_skip.residual_follow_up: The STATIC layer (hook-wiring-parity.bats) checks basename symmetry but does NOT assert a committed settings.json lacks disableAllHooks:true. A repo could commit wiring+disableAllHooks:true and pass both layers — but that is a born-disabled config visible in review as a literal field, not a weakened-from-protected regression. Low-severity static-layer follow-up.

completeness_test_limits.keyword_and_type_gate: SCHEMA_SET = properties where type=='boolean' AND description matches /hook/i. A future hook-killer that is (a) non-boolean (e.g. anyOf like strictPluginOnlyCustomization, which mentions blocking customization surfaces and could gate hooks in managed settings) or (b) disables hooks without the word 'hook' (e.g. a hypothetical 'disableAutomation') would ESCAPE the completeness check and the guard would not cover it. On the CURRENT schema (2.1.217) there is NO such uncovered boolean hook-killer — the only two (disableAllHooks, allowManagedHooksOnly) are both covered. So this is a future-schema risk, not a present open vector.
completeness_test_limits.ci_skip: Schema absent -> the test SKIPs with an explicit message (not a silent pass). Better than silent, but the 'schema forces registration' guarantee only fires on a machine with the claude-code VSCode/Cursor extension installed. In the recorded run the schema WAS present and test 77 PASSED (executed, not skipped). The runtime guard's hard-coded list still enforces the two known switches everywhere regardless.
completeness_test_limits.guard_set_extraction: grep -oE 'HOOK_KILL_SWITCHES="..."' is test-only and robust for the single-line assignment; a multi-line refactor would break the grep and FAIL the test (safe direction). Not a security boundary.
completeness_test_limits.moving_target_note: The schema updated 2.1.215->217 during this session; `sort -V | tail -1` correctly tracks the newest. The completeness test therefore validates against whatever Anthropic ships next — good, and confirmed working.
